column1: *** CORDOBA - THE PARISH REGISTERS ARE NOT ON FAMILYSEARCH ***
column2: *** The FamilySearch Research Wiki page for Cordoba Province lists, under CHURCH RECORDS, no FamilySearch collection at all *** - only MyHeritage indexes of municipal births, deaths and marriages, behind a paywall. The province *** belongs to the Diocese of Cordoba *** and the registers are with the diocese. What FamilySearch does have is *** 'Spain, Cordoba, Municipal Records, 1509-1947' - index and images ***.
column4: *** SO SANCHO'S BAPTISM IS NOT SITTING ON A FAMILYSEARCH FILM WAITING TO BE ADDRESSED BY NUMBER. *** The Municipal Records collection was searched for Llerena in Cordoba: *** 5,031 results, and every one visible is a municipal CENSUS of 1919-1924. *** Its 1509 start date is not where its indexed content is. *** The route to an eighteenth-century Cordoba baptism is the diocesan archive, which is a letter, not a search. ***

column1: *** ASTURIAS - THE SAME, WITH ONE PARTIAL EXCEPTION ***
column2: *** Asturias belongs to the Diocese of Oviedo. *** The wiki lists one FamilySearch church collection: *** 'Spain, Diocese of SANTANDER, Catholic Church Records, 1538-1985 - contains SOME records for Asturias' ***, index and images. Plus *** 'Spain, Asturias, Municipal Records, 1470-1897' ***.
column4: *** PARTIAL COVERAGE OF THE WRONG DIOCESE IS STILL WORTH SEARCHING *** - Rodrigo and Rosa Fernandez are the least-searched people in this archive and have never been looked for in Spain at all. *** But it is not a substitute for Oviedo's own registers. ***

column1: *** AND THE CORRECTION TO THIS SESSION'S OWN PESSIMISM ***
column2: *** The wiki's provincial pages are NOT the whole picture. *** A record search for Llerena in Spain, 1730-1800, returns *** 228 results *** drawn from national collections the Cordoba page never mentions: *** 'Spain, Catholic Church Records, 1307-2005' ***, *** 'Spain, Baptisms, 1502-1940' ***, *** 'Spain, Marriages, 1565-1950' *** and *** 'Spain, Granada, Catholic Pre-Marriage Investigation Files, 1556-1899' ***.
column4: *** SO THE EIGHTEENTH CENTURY IS REACHABLE BY INDEX EVEN WHERE IT IS NOT REACHABLE BY IMAGE. *** That is a different answer from the one this session was heading towards an hour ago. *** Note especially the Granada PRE-MARRIAGE INVESTIGATION FILES, 1556-1899 *** - the same record type that was walked at Canelones this morning, indexed, for Andalusia, covering the right century.

column1: *** THE LEAD: A DOCUMENT THIS ARCHIVE ALREADY CLOSED, WHICH THE 1791 ACT RE-OPENS ***
column2: *** 'Sancho de Lerena y Armenta, married 17 November 1754, Granada, to ANA MARIA DE AGUILAR. Birth: CORDOBA. Parents: Sancho de Lerena y Velasco and Maria Antonia de Armenta y Guebara.' *** Indexed in Spain, Marriages 1565-1950 and in the Granada pre-marriage files.
column4: *** THIS ARCHIVE FOUND THAT ACT, EXAMINED IT, AND CORRECTLY SET IT ASIDE *** - it settles Cordoba versus Granada *** for the 1754 groom, not for the Uruguayan Sancho ***, and this archive has already had to correct itself once for overstating exactly that. *** WHAT HAS CHANGED IS THE OTHER SIDE OF THE COMPARISON. *** On 8 January 1791 the Canelones act gave our Sancho's parents as *** FELIX LLERENA and ROSALIA AGUILAR, naturales de dicha Cordova ***. So there are now *** TWO Lerena-Aguilar unions in Cordoba and Granada in the same generation ***, and *** the given name SANCHO recurring across them ***. *** THAT IS NOT PROOF AND IS NOT BEING TREATED AS ANY. *** It is a reason to re-open a file that was closed before the parents were known, and to look for a marriage of Felix Llerena and Rosalia Aguilar in the same Granada and Cordoba indexes.
